newsitem.title: UK: Patten "warily optimistic" over HK under China.
newsitem.headline: Patten "warily optimistic" over HK under China.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten has expressed "wary optimism" over the future of Hong Kong when it reverts to China later this year, saying its people would not allow their civic consciousness to be "turned out like a light".

In an article published by the London Guardian newspaper on Saturday, Patten wrote of his frustration over the provisional legislature picked by a Chinese-appointed panel and China's plans to roll back civil liberties in the former British colony after the handover on July 1.
But Patten added; "Despite all the problems and inevitable difficulties, am I warily optimistic about Hong Kong's future?

"Yes, because this is a city in its prime, with the potential to be even more successful -- the New York of Asia. I cannot believe that the people of Hong Kong will be prepared to let that opportunity slip from their grasp."
Patten said the people of Hong Kong were proud of having turned a rather closed, colonial city into an open, international centre.
"Their civic consciousness is not going to be turned out like a light at midnight on June 30," he wrote.

Patten said Britain's parliament would hear reports every six months following the handover to Beijing on the implementation of the Joint Declaration agreed by China and Britain which guarantees Hong Kong's way of life for another 50 years.
He said Britain would also be working closely with the United States, Canada and other allies in urging China to meet its obligations.
